result.title: Steering Vectors for Competing Ethical Frameworks Are Interchangeable: A Competing-Target Test for Activation Steering
result.summary: Activation steering adds a vector to a model's hidden states to control a named behaviour. A gain on that behaviour, however, does not show that the vector controls it directly: it may act through a component shared with neighbouring behaviours, which unsteered and random baselines cannot separate. We introduce the competing-target test: a vector is compared with the vector built the same way for a competing target, and an equivalence test states when their difference is below a useful margin. We apply it in open-weight models to vectors for Kantian deontology, which judges an act by the rule it follows, and act utilitarianism, which judges it by the welfare it produces. On held-out situations, prompting a framework raises its score and lowers the other's, whereas vectors for either framework move both scores alike, and none reaches the margin. The two vectors share most of their direction, a request to apply some framework; the same construction separates an optimistic from a pessimistic tone, whose vectors share much less. What a vector shares with its competitors therefore sets what it controls: steering a perspective can deliver a mixture, and measuring a disposition can measure its neighbours, unless tested against the competing target.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「竞争目标检验」，在开源权重模型中对康德义务论与行为功利主义两种伦理框架的激活引导向量做等价性比较，发现两个向量方向高度重合、共享的只是「套用某种框架」这一成分，因而按目标命名的引导并不特异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「竞争目标对照+等价性判据」可能为核查 LVR 中 latent 状态究竟携带任务必要视觉内容、还是坍缩为可被邻近行为共用的泛化方向（如信息坍缩、贡献分配）提供方法线索，但需人工核查该因果归因套路能否迁移到多模态推理状态。
